components.name: Operational Data Table
components.purpose: Compare identifiable records and act on an explicitly scoped result set without confusing missing data, permission or selection.
useWhen: Several records share meaningful comparable attributes.
Operators need stable identity, sorting or scoped row and bulk actions.
avoidWhen: A narrative, product discovery gallery or a single detail view is the main task.
Spreadsheet editing or spatial scheduling requires a dedicated grid or calendar contract.

visual.hierarchy: Collection identity and current scope precede column headings; record identifier anchors each row before secondary metadata.
visual.alignment: Align text to reading direction and comparable numbers to the trailing edge; align headers with their cell values.
visual.spacing: Use the same horizontal inset for caption, toolbar and first content column; separate bulk actions from row controls.
visual.typography: Use body text for values, a restrained header weight and secondary text for metadata; tabular numerals support comparisons where available.
visual.emphasis: Reserve strongest emphasis for record identity and the current task action; selection uses an additional labeled marker.
visual.surfaces: Use subtle row separators for tracking across columns; avoid a separate elevated card around every cell.
visual.proportions: Give identity and long names flexible width; keep status and numeric columns readable; wrap important names or expose full text accessibly.
visual.discoverability: Keep the frequent row action visible; name overflow controls with record identity and show bulk controls with selected count.
visual.states: Show missing as unknown or unavailable rather than zero; status includes words, freshness and units where relevant.
visual.brand: Reuse existing text, border, status and focus tokens; do not invent an industry palette.

keyboard.result: Visit links, selection and actions in document order; cells are read through table navigation.
keyboard.focus: Visible control focus; no custom arrow interception.

keyboard.focus: Retain control or nearest surviving row action.

keyboard.when: Only when a separately implemented and tested interactive grid is explicitly chosen.
keyboard.result: Use the complete APG grid focus model; this table pilot does not supply editable-cell behavior.

accessibility.naming: Give the region a task-specific heading and each control a persistent name.
accessibility.semantics: Prefer native table, caption and associated headers. Sort uses a button and aria-sort on its header. Checkboxes have record-specific names. A selectable table remains a table; an interactive grid is a separate composite-widget implementation requiring managed arrow-key focus.

responsive.focusContinuity: Keep selected IDs and sort state; restore focus to the same record action after detail navigation, or the collection heading if removed.
